newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-GAUTENG LIONS SET THE PACE IN SUPER 12.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-GAUTENG LIONS SET THE PACE IN SUPER 12.

text.p: Transvaal may have become the Gauteng Lions at the beginning of the week but the name change appears to have had no ill effect on Kobus Wiese's men in rugby union's Super 12 competition.
After beating New South Wales 36-27 on Saturday the Lions now top the standings after four rounds of the Southern hemisphere showpiece.
In a competition where bonus points are awarded for tries and close results, they have dropped only two points and have 18 in all. It leaves them with a six-point lead over ACT and Waikato.
Defending champions Auckland have a game in hand and have 11 points from three games.
The Lions scored three tries in their Ellis Park victory on Saturday but were again thankful to the boot of Gavin "Magic" Johnson who kicked 19 points in addition to scoring one of the tries.

The Lions have two more home games before they have to leave South African shores and they could have all but wrapped up a semifinal spot by then if they can gather maximum points against Wellington and Northern Transvaal. That would give them 28 points and from then on a point a game would probably be good enough.

But Springbok scrum-half Johan Roux adopted a cautious stance when he said: "We are going overseas not to get one point a game, but to win. If you want to be Super 12 champions you have to prove that you can win away from home."

The surprise of the weekend came earlier in the day when last year's beaten finalists Natal went down 45-40 to Free State in Bloemfontein. Natal were criticised for resting some key players and they paid the price of over-confidence with their first defeat.
Free State were outscored by five tries to three but fly-half M.J. Smith sealed the win with a haul of eight penalties to punish Natal's indiscipline.

In New Zealand, Waikato piled on the misery for Queensland who went down 31-16 -- their fourth straight defeat. It was Waikato's third win in four starts, but for the Reds coach John Connolly it's back to the drawing board.

Otago took advantage of a below strength Northern Transvaal team to post a 27-7 win in Dunedin. The Blue Bulls were without star backs Joost van der Westhuizen, Andre Snyman and Jacques Olivier, all with the national side at the World Sevens in Hong Kong. All Black fly-half Simon Culhane was on target for the Highlanders, kicking 15 of his side's points.

At Bruce Stadium in Canberra, Australian Capital Territory got back on track with a 49-29 win over Canterbury. After losing their last game to the Lions, the Brumbies were back to their best with flank forward Ipolito Fenukitau scoring a hat trick of tries.
